ctx.x: You'd say Basher was right at the top though, would you?

He was top, yeah. He was, he was wonderful. And that Basher could take, I remember that, Buddy Petit and them on top. They hired him to play the advertising. And at that time Bob Lyons was working in the pawn shop on Ramport and Pedita. Bob Lyons, the bass player. And Basher didn't have no clarinet. I remember this, I recall that good girl, I used to follow all the bands. So they said we're going to get him a clarinet. The wagon pulls up with the horse in it, up at a pawn shop and they told, told Bob Lyons that…
Yeah, the brown one. I've seen it.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: Bob Lyne, you know, Bob Lyne was an Eagle Band all these days

ctx.x: Well, if I can recall at that time, I can call some of the guys, I think. Bob Lyne, you know, Bob Lyne was an Eagle Band all these days, most of all these days. Frankie Deuce and they had Chiff on trumpet. I think they had Lil' Warnick on the clarinet. And Danny Lewis on. No, it wasn't Danny Lewis. Danny Lewis came in the Eagle Band later on after Bob Lyne left. Now, who was the drummer? I can't recall. I don't know if it was Hennerzine or Hennerzine. I don't know, I can't recall who was the drummer. Guitar?

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: Had, uh, Bob Lyons on bass.

ctx.x: If you could run through that, do you remember? Yeah, I heard them.

Well, Imperial Band, when I heard them, they had that which was, Manny Paracis, was the lead of that band. And he had Buddy Johnson on trombone at that time. And he had Baby Matthews on drums. And he had George Buckhead on clarinet. And Willie Santiago on the guitar. And Jimmy Brown played the bass. That was Imperial Band. The Superior Band. The Superior Band. Now, pardon me. The Superior Band, in that band, I, when I first seen that band, they had, uh, uh, uh, Mac Murray on drums. They had, uh, Cock and Rumble…
